- *Why no figure exists:* Nobody asked for publication and none was needed - the documents were filed in answer to court orders and the judgment reproduces none of the numbers. Their authors are named and their contents are described by the Court. The dataset is not missing; it is in a case file that a court closed in March 2020.
- *What would close it:* Certified copies from the registry of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir at Srinagar, as above.

**L-0114** (ledger) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* The Divisional Commissioner Kashmir's list of persons identified as permanently or partially disabled, and the criteria applied
- *Why no figure exists:* Sixty-four people were paid on the strength of this list by two named government orders of 5 January and 26 February 2018, so the list plainly exists. No reason for its non-publication has ever been stated.
- *What would close it:* An RTI to the Divisional Commissioner, Kashmir for the list submitted by communications dated 23 October 2017 and 25 January 2018 pursuant to Government Order No.61-Home of 2017, and for the criteria applied in classifying permanent and partial disablement. Every element of this route - office, document, date and authorising order - is named in a retrieved judgment.

**L-0114** (ledger) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Injuries caused by crowd-control munitions other than pellets - tear-smoke, PAVA and plastic pellets
- *Why no figure exists:* No body has acknowledged the category and no official series of any kind was located. Unlike pellets there is not even a refused parliamentary question specific to it: the 2018 question asked for PAVA consumption, not PAVA injuries.

**L-0116** (ledger) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* The findings of magisterial inquiries into contested killings in Jammu and Kashmir
- *Why no figure exists:* The Hyderpora inquiry was ordered by the Lieutenant Governor on 18 November 2021 with a fifteen-day deadline; families met him on 7 December 2021 and he sought two days to publish it; it has never appeared. Classified not-published rather than withheld on the written test, which turns on producibility under compulsion and not on whether anyone asked: no requester issued a request and no authority issued a refusal. What is recorded is a promise volunteered by the holder and not kept, which is non-release. For the general figure of 506 inquiries since 1990 the position is weaker still and no request-and-refusal is documented at all. Demoted from withheld on 2026-08-03 in the pre-merge verification of this phase, on the same test that demoted two education-phase absences.
- *What would close it:* An RTI to the District Magistrate, Srinagar for the report of the magisterial inquiry into the Hyderpora encounter of 15 November 2021 conducted by the Additional District Magistrate, and a parallel RTI to the District Magistrate, Ganderbal for the 2026 inquiry report.

**L-0116** (ledger) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* The number of bodies buried away from home districts under the practice, year-wise
- *Why no figure exists:* No body has published a series. Three counts attributed to official sources circulate and do not reconcile, and none has an established basis.
- *What would close it:* A parliamentary question to MHA for the year-wise number of persons killed in encounters in J&K whose bodies were buried at locations other than their home districts since 1 April 2020, and the number subsequently exhumed and handed over.

**L-0117** (ledger) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* A defined, published, year-wise count of J&K residents joining militant organisations
- *Why no figure exists:* Zero occurrences in seventeen MHA Annual Reports and in every parliamentary reply retrieved, and no body has explained why a quantity it describes itself as managing is not published. The state plainly holds something - officials quote figures - but has never published a return, and the internal inconsistency of what is quoted shows it is not a maintained series.
- *What would close it:* A parliamentary question to MHA for the year-wise number of J&K residents recorded as having joined militant organisations, with the definition used, and asking expressly whether persons categorised as hybrid militants are included. The definitional rider is what makes this worth filing; the bare number would reproduce the existing confusion.

**L-0117** (ledger) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* The local and foreign composition of militants killed in J&K, for the entire post-2001 period
- *Why no figure exists:* MHA has never published the split in any Annual Report. SATP published it from 1990 and stopped on 15 November 2001, dropping with it the stated qualifier that the data covered only identified militants killed. The split is the single most-used measure in the argument about whether militancy is indigenous or externally supplied, and it is quoted constantly and measured nowhere.
- *What would close it:* A parliamentary question to MHA for the year-wise disaggregation of the 'Terrorists killed' column of its own Annual Report table into local and foreign nationals.

**L-0118** (ledger) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* The organised stone-pelting series in MHA's flagship instrument
- *Why no figure exists:* No stone-pelting or law-and-order incident table has ever appeared in the J&K section of any MHA Annual Report, while the Annual Report 2024-25 asserts the conclusion drawn from the series in prose. MHA holds the data and produced it on request in July 2024, so the omission from the flagship is an editorial choice and not a data gap.
- *What would close it:* A parliamentary question to MHA for the full year-wise organised stone-pelting and hartal series rather than the three sampled years - the identical route that produced the reply of 24 July 2024, which is the strongest route in the phase because it has already worked once.

**L-0118** (ledger) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Any independent measure of political grievance in J&K not mediated by the state
- *Why no figure exists:* Both sides of this dispute argue from the state's own data, and no unmanipulated protest-event dataset, independent attitude survey or independent reading of the 2024 mandate was located. This is the one factual gap that could discriminate between the two accounts.

**L-0119** (ledger) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Infiltration attempts and net estimated infiltration into J&K for 2023 onward
- *Why no figure exists:* MHA published the table in every Annual Report from at least 2010-11 through 2022-23 and discontinued it without announcing or explaining the discontinuation, while the border-management apparatus that generates the count continues to operate and is described at length in the same reports.
- *What would close it:* A parliamentary question to MHA for year-wise infiltration attempts and net estimated infiltration for 2023, 2024 and 2025 - a request to resume a series the Ministry itself published for over a decade. A parallel question to the Ministry of Defence would test whether the Army holds it independently.

**L-0119** (ledger) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Whether 'Successful', 'Net infiltration (Estimated)' and 'Net Estimated infiltration' are the same quantity, and how an infiltration attempt is detected and counted
- *Why no figure exists:* The row label changed four times between the Annual Reports 2013-14 and 2017-18 and no report has ever said whether the quantities are the same. 'Net Estimated' is labelled an estimate; 'Infiltration attempts' is not, and no MHA document states the detection or counting rule for an attempt.
- *What would close it:* The same RTI to the Department of Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh Affairs for the compiling instructions and proforma behind the J&K returns would answer this alongside the incident definitions.

**L-0120** (ledger) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* The cumulative total of deaths in the J&K conflict since 1990, updated beyond 2020
- *Why no figure exists:* MHA published it in the opening sentence of the J&K section for at least thirteen consecutive report years and discontinued it from the Annual Report 2021-22 without stating a reason. The components are still published annually.
- *What would close it:* A parliamentary question to MHA for the cumulative figure updated to the current year. It is trivially answerable from MHA's own published rows, which makes a refusal informative in itself.

**L-0120** (ledger) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* A cumulative count of militants killed in J&K since 1990
- *Why no figure exists:* The cumulative ledger never had a militants-killed term in any of the thirty years it was published, so no official cumulative total of conflict deaths has ever existed - only of two of the three populations. Nothing was ever gathered for the third.

**L-0121** (ledger) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Deaths in the custody of the Army, Rashtriya Rifles, CRPF, BSF or any other central armed police force in J&K
- *Why no figure exists:* There is no category, column, row or footnote for it anywhere in NCRB's custodial-crimes chapter, whose unit of account is the State or UT police; the NHRC's 24-hour intimation regime is addressed only to District Magistrates and Superintendents of Police; and section 19 of the PHRA leaves the Commission unable to investigate those forces in any event. The quantity has nowhere to be recorded.

**L-0121** (ledger) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* The ~630 complaints pending before the J&K State Human Rights Commission on 31 October 2019
- *Why no figure exists:* The Commission's enabling statute was repealed with no transitional or savings provision, so the complaints abated. Their records are reported to have been physically locked in the former premises since that date.
- *What would close it:* An RTI to the J&K General Administration Department for the disposal status and custody of the former State Human Rights Commission's records. The correct addressee could not be verified because jkhome.nic.in was unreachable.

**L-0121** (ledger) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Deaths of J&K detenus held in prisons outside the territory
- *Why no figure exists:* NCRB's unit of account is the State or UT that holds the body, so a J&K Public Safety Act detenu who dies in a prison in another State is recorded, if at all, as a judicial-custody death of that State and is severed from J&K entirely. One such death is documented - a detenu who died in Naini jail, Prayagraj, on 23 December 2019, whose family learned of it only afterwards. This is a second structural hole of the same family as the entry above and is not covered by it: that one is about Army and central-force custody, this one is about the territorial attribution of a death in ordinary judicial custody.

**L-0122** (ledger) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* The procedure, norms, criteria and standards applied in deciding an AFSPA section 7 sanction request
- *Why no figure exists:* Both the Ministry of Defence and Army Headquarters stated on the record, in answer to a statutory information request, that they do not hold it, and the Commission required an affidavit to that effect. The holders have attested that it does not exist in documentary form, so there is nothing to release.

**L-0122** (ledger) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* AFSPA section 7 sanction requests received, granted, refused and pending in respect of J&K since 1 January 2019
- *Why no figure exists:* The published figures end at April 2018 and no later statement was located from either ministry.
- *What would close it:* A parliamentary question to the Ministry of Defence and to MHA for sanction requests received, granted, refused and pending in respect of J&K since 1 January 2019.

**L-0122** (ledger) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* The areas of J&K notified as disturbed under the AFSPA (J&K) Act 1990, and the dates of the notifications in force
- *Why no figure exists:* The 1990 Act is never named in any MHA Annual Report retrieved and no disturbed-area statement for J&K appears in any of them, while the equivalent information for AFSPA 1958 in the North East is volunteered annually at district granularity. MHA administers the Act and the notifications are its own instruments.
- *What would close it:* A parliamentary question to MHA for the areas of J&K currently notified as disturbed under the AFSPA (J&K) Act 1990 with the dates of the notifications in force - framed on the asymmetry with what MHA publishes for the North East without being asked.

**L-0123** (ledger) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Whether the Lieutenant Governor has made rules under the proviso to section 46(1) clause (c) of the Reorganisation Act
- *Why no figure exists:* The reporting that raised the power in January 2025 was prospective, and the October 2025 refusal was justified by reference to departmental jurisdiction rather than to any rules made. A bar arising from made rules and a bar arising from the Speaker's own construction of legislative competence are different things with different routes to challenge, and no document establishing which is operating was located.
- *What would close it:* An RTI to the Secretary, J&K Legislative Assembly for any rules made under the proviso to section 46(1) of the J&K Reorganisation Act 2019 and the date of the Speaker's consultation. The addressee could not be verified in this phase.

**L-0124** (ledger) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Perpetrator attribution for civilian deaths in Jammu and Kashmir after 2019
- *Why no figure exists:* The only body that ever published it ceased to publish, and no official instrument has ever carried the quantity: MHA's column merges the two causes and names neither, GTD covers non-state perpetrators only by construction, and UCDP records no Government-of-India one-sided violence anywhere in India after 2002.
- *What would close it:* A dedicated assessment of Kashmir Law and Justice Project, which is publishing monthly and is the only identified live candidate successor; and, failing that, a registered ACLED export, which can in principle carry perpetrator attribution for India from 1 January 2016.

**L-0012** (ledger) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Revenue buoyancy under GST against the 14 per cent growth the guarantee assumed
- *Why no figure exists:* The case against asserts the buoyancy promise was never clearly met and gives no figure; this record carries collections in levels, not a buoyancy ratio against a base. The Department of Revenue and the GST Council between them hold the series needed to compute it. Entered 2026-08-05 when the assessment note was written and the claim was found to be argued without a measure.
- *What would close it:* A Department of Revenue or GST Council statement of buoyancy by year against the pre-GST base, or the underlying revenue and nominal-GDP series on a consistent definition.

**L-0012** (ledger) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Compliance cost borne by taxpayers, and its distribution by firm size
- *Why no figure exists:* The claim at launch was simpler compliance and the case against holds that cost fell hardest on smaller firms. Neither is quantified anywhere in this record. No official estimate of GST compliance cost by firm size was retrieved.
- *What would close it:* An official or peer-reviewed estimate of compliance cost by turnover band.

**L-0016** (ledger) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Manufacturing jobs created against the 100 million announced
- *Why no figure exists:* Announced alongside the share target and measured nowhere in this record. India has no employment series that isolates manufacturing jobs attributable to a policy programme, and the periodic labour force survey measures sectoral employment without attribution. Entered 2026-08-05 when the assessment note was written and the target was found to be unscored.

**L-0017** (ledger) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Imports displaced by production under the schemes, by sector
- *Why no figure exists:* Import substitution was an announced objective and no figure for it appears in this record. Sectoral import series exist, but attributing a change in them to the incentive rather than to tariff changes, exchange rates or global supply shifts has no agreed construction, and no official estimate was retrieved.

**L-0078** (ledger) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Attacks on journalists
- *Why no figure exists:* The Minister of Information and Broadcasting confirmed in Parliament that the NCRB does not maintain separate data on attacks on journalists. Recorded as a straightforward absence: no evidence reviewed contradicts the stated position. Its effect is that the government's rejection of external indices is not accompanied by an internal series that could be compared against them.

**L-0081** (ledger) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Official count of internet shutdowns
- *Why no figure exists:* No central register of shutdown orders is published, and the Ministry of Home Affairs has now said so itself twice on the record. Rajya Sabha Unstarred Question No. 1791, answered 10 March 2021, verbatim: "Centralized data of internet shutdown is not maintained by the Ministry of Home affairs. Orders issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) are available at MHA website." The second sentence is a real limit and travels with the first: the Union does publish its own orders. What it does not maintain is centralised data across the federal boundary. The mechanism is stated by the Ministry in the Standing Committee on Communications and Information Technology's 26th Report of December 2021 at para 26: a national counting apparatus exists, internet suspension was classified outside its ambit, and there is no proposal in MHA to collect this information at a central level. This upgrades the classification from inference to admission; it does not disturb not-collected.

**L-0083** (ledger) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* UAPA cases booked against journalists
- *Why no figure exists:* The Ministry of Home Affairs told Parliament in December 2024 that data on cases booked under the UAPA against journalists is not maintained by the NCRB. Recorded as a straightforward absence. Its effect is that the question of whether the Act is applied to journalists cannot be answered from official data in either direction, which forecloses the government's defence as much as the critics' charge. Pairs with the NCRB absence on attacks on journalists recorded at L-0078.

**L-0034** (ledger) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Household air pollution and the health burden it imposes, before and after connection
- *Why no figure exists:* The announced purpose of the scheme. No population-scale measurement of exposure or of the health outcomes it drives appears in this record or in anything retrieved; refill counts are a proxy for fuel use, not a measure of health. Entered 2026-08-05 when the note was written and the objective was found unscored.

**L-0034** (ledger) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Biomass displaced per household, as distinct from cylinders delivered
- *Why no figure exists:* The case for holds that supplementary LPG use still displaces some biomass, which is plausible and unquantified. Refill frequency bounds it loosely at best, and no fuel-stacking measurement at national scale was retrieved.

**L-0035** (ledger) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Open-defecation behaviour at national scale from an instrument independent of the implementing ministry
- *Why no figure exists:* The independent panel evidence covers four states; the national figure comes from the ministry's own survey, which the panel's findings contradict where the two overlap. No national-scale independent behavioural measurement was retrieved, so the size of the divergence outside those four states is unknown.
- *What would close it:* A national household survey measuring defecation practice person-by-person, fielded independently of the implementing ministry.

**L-0036** (ledger) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Functionality - water meeting Mission standards in quantity and quality - across all covered rural households rather than in certified villages
- *Why no figure exists:* The 2024 assessment covers 19,812 certified villages, which is a subset chosen on certification status. The national figure it is routinely read as is not what it measures, and no all-India functionality measurement was retrieved. The Ministry runs the certification and holds the underlying returns.
- *What would close it:* A Ministry of Jal Shakti functionality assessment on a sample representative of all covered households, or the state-wise functionality returns published in full.

**L-0037** (ledger) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Completed houses actually occupied
- *Why no figure exists:* This record asserts a gap between completion and occupation and gives no figure for it. Completion is reported by the implementing ministries through their own management systems, which record construction stage rather than residence, and no occupancy measurement was retrieved. Entered 2026-08-05 when the note was written.
- *What would close it:* A Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs or Ministry of Rural Development occupancy survey of completed units, or a Comptroller and Auditor General audit sampling completed houses for residence.

**L-0038** (ledger) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Hunger or food insecurity among the covered population, before and during the transfers
- *Why no figure exists:* Preventing hunger was the stated purpose. This record measures grain moved and money spent, which are inputs. No population-scale food-insecurity measurement covering the period appears here or in anything retrieved.

**L-0038** (ledger) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* An official estimate of the number of people excluded from the statutory entitlement by the use of 2011 census ratios
- *Why no figure exists:* The exclusion figures in this record are scholarly estimates. The Department of Food and Public Distribution holds the coverage ratios and current population projections and can compute the shortfall directly; no official figure was retrieved.
- *What would close it:* A Department of Food and Public Distribution statement of entitled population against covered population on current projections, or a Parliamentary answer giving both.

**L-0039** (ledger) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Incidence of catastrophic health expenditure among covered households, before and after enrolment
- *Why no figure exists:* This is the stated objective and the record measures admissions and aggregate out-of-pocket share instead. Neither isolates the covered population, and no before-and-after measurement of catastrophic expenditure among beneficiaries was retrieved. The National Health Authority holds enrolment and claims data and the household expenditure surveys exist separately; nothing links them in published form.
- *What would close it:* A National Health Authority or National Sample Survey study of out-of-pocket and catastrophic expenditure among enrolled households against a comparable uncovered group.

**L-0040** (ledger) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* MGNREGA work demanded but not recorded
- *Why no figure exists:* The scheme is demand-driven but only work PROVIDED is counted; suppressed demand leaves no trace in the series, so rationing and falling need are indistinguishable in the data. Reclassified never-defined to not-collected on 2026-08-01: the quantity is defined and the denominator is defined; what is missing is collection on that base, not an agreed definition.
- *What would close it:* Independent demand surveys; LibTech's registration-versus-delivery divergence is the closest available proxy

**L-0041** (ledger) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Farmer household income after 2018-19
- *Why no figure exists:* No Situation Assessment Survey has been conducted since 2019, so the 2022 doubling target cannot be evaluated against the only authoritative instrument.
- *What would close it:* A post-2019 NSSO Situation Assessment Survey of Agricultural Households

**aser-std3-reading** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Learning outcomes of urban children
- *Why no figure exists:* ASER is a rural household survey and has no regular urban round. India has no independent household-based learning measurement for its urban children at all, and roughly a third of Indians live in towns and cities.
- *What would close it:* A regular urban ASER, or an independent household-based urban learning assessment

**aser-std3-reading** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Adjustment for the fall in underage entry to Standard I
- *Why no figure exists:* The share of children aged 5 or under in Standard I fell from 25.6 per cent (2018) to 16.7 per cent (2024). ASER tests by grade, not by age, so an older Standard III cohort raises expected ability mechanically. Nobody has adjusted for it and it could be a material share of the Standard III gain.
- *What would close it:* An age-standardised recut of ASER's own microdata, which ASER holds

**aser-std3-reading** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Learning at any point during the school closures of 2020-2022
- *Why no figure exists:* No field ASER and no government learning assessment was conducted between November 2018 and November 2022. Nothing exists that compulsion could produce, because nobody was in the field.

**nas-parakh-grade3-language** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Standard errors on any PARAKH 2024 figure
- *Why no figure exists:* The National Report carries point estimates to the whole percentage point with no uncertainty anywhere. NAS Cycle 3 published standard errors; PARAKH 2024 does not - a regression in reporting practice.
- *What would close it:* A psychometric technical report; the file PARAKH publishes under that name is a 274 MB rasterised image file containing no extractable psychometrics

**nas-parakh-grade3-language** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* The test-day absentee rate and the characteristics of replaced students
- *Why no figure exists:* PARAKH's own Operational Guidelines instruct the Field Investigator that 'if selected students are absent then move to the next student'. There is no absentee count field, no non-response flag and no non-response weight, so the absentee rate is destroyed at the point of collection and is unrecoverable in principle. The published score is conditioned on attendance and the conditioning is nowhere documented. ASER's school visits put daily attendance in government primary schools at 72.4 (2018) to 75.9 (2024) per cent.

**nas-parakh-grade3-language** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Student-level microdata for any NAS or PARAKH round
- *Why no figure exists:* The PARAKH FAQ states that 'NAS does not provide individual school or student scores'. Without it, standardised measures of within-instrument change cannot be constructed from the published aggregates.
- *What would close it:* A research-access request to NCERT/PARAKH for anonymised student-level NAS and PARAKH files. The PARAKH FAQ states individual scores are not provided - a standing non-release policy, not a response to a request.

**nas-parakh-grade3-language** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* The test items used in any NAS or PARAKH round
- *Why no figure exists:* NAS does not make public the test questions it uses; PARAKH publishes sample items only. This is an identifiable standing refusal rather than mere non-release.
- *What would close it:* An RTI to NCERT for the NAS and PARAKH item banks. Item security is a defensible ground for refusal, since released items cannot be reused for trend measurement, so this request may correctly fail. A refusal is what would make `withheld` the right value; it is not the right value now, because no refusal has been sought.

**nas-parakh-grade3-language** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* A re-run of the Johnson-Parrado state-correlation test on PARAKH 2024
- *Why no figure exists:* For NAS 2017, state rankings correlated at +0.19 with ASER, -0.03 with an independent household survey and +0.05 with state income, against a +0.82 benchmark - the finding that NAS carries almost no information about relative state performance. Whether the CBSE administration reforms fixed it has never been tested. The test is computable today from published PARAKH state figures, published ASER 2024 state figures and net state domestic product. It is the highest-value missing analysis in the domain.
- *What would close it:* A published correlation of PARAKH 2024 state means against ASER 2024 state means and NSDP per capita

**nas-parakh-grade3-language** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Reconciliation of PARAKH's two official sample counts
- *Why no figure exists:* The National Report says 74,229 schools and 21,15,022 students across 781 districts; PARAKH's own landing page says 75,565 schools and over 2,294,377 students across 782 districts. About 8 per cent of the intended student sample is unaccounted for between two PARAKH sources, and PARAKH nowhere says which is sampled and which realised.
- *What would close it:* A request to PARAKH for the achieved sample by district for the 2024 round. The results were computed from an achieved sample, so a figure exists; the two published counts differ by about 8 per cent of students and one district.

**nas-parakh-grade3-maths** (series) · `not-published`

- *Why no figure exists:* The National Report carries point estimates to the whole percentage point with no uncertainty anywhere. NAS Cycle 3 published standard errors; PARAKH 2024 does not - a regression in reporting practice.

**parakh-grade9-maths** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Any independent measurement of secondary-stage learning in India
- *Why no figure exists:* No household-based or independent instrument assesses grade-level competency above the primary stage. India has also not participated in any international large-scale assessment in recent years, and NAS 2021 has not been linked to any global scale.
- *What would close it:* Participation in PISA, TIMSS or PIRLS, or an independent secondary-stage household assessment

**parakh-grade3-proficient-language** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* The PARAKH 2024 proficiency-band cut-scores
- *Why no figure exists:* Not published in the National Report, the FAQ, the Operational Guidelines or the document PARAKH publishes as a technical report. Without them the headline 18-point and 23-point gains cannot be audited, and the language/mathematics inversion proves the cuts sit at different distributional points.
- *What would close it:* Publication of the band definitions and cut-scores, which PARAKH must hold in order to have computed the bands

**parakh-grade3-proficient-maths** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* The PARAKH 2024 proficiency-band cut-scores
- *Why no figure exists:* Not published in the National Report, the FAQ, the Operational Guidelines or the document PARAKH publishes as a technical report. Without them the headline 18-point and 23-point gains cannot be audited, and the language/mathematics inversion proves the cuts sit at different distributional points.
- *What would close it:* Publication of the band definitions and cut-scores, which PARAKH must hold in order to have computed the bands

**school-closure-weeks-covid** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* State-by-state and grade-by-grade closure duration for India
- *Why no figure exists:* Closure in India was decided by states and differentiated by grade, and 'partially open' covers everything from one grade in one state shut to all primary grades shut across most of the country. Neither UNESCO nor the Government of India published a state-wise or grade-wise closure-duration series.
- *What would close it:* A compiled record of state school-reopening orders 2020-2022, which the states issued and the Union could have collated

**school-closure-weeks-covid** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Any Indian government statement of a national school-closure duration
- *Why no figure exists:* No Indian government document stating a national closure duration was retrieved. Candidate not-published pending a parliamentary-reply search.
- *What would close it:* A targeted search of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha replies on school-closure duration 2020-2022, and of MoE circulars for the period. A nil result means the reasonKind is wrong: closure was a state decision and no national figure may ever have been computed.

**school-enrolment-total-udise** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* How much of the enrolment fall is deduplication and how much is real decline
- *Why no figure exists:* No back-cast, no dual-basis year and no reconciliation table appears in any UDISE+ report. The ministry's position is purely declarative: pre-2021-22 and post-2022-23 are two series and may not be joined. It holds both the old and the new bases and could produce a dual run for one year.
- *What would close it:* A single year published on both bases, or a published decomposition of the 1.34 crore records removed

**single-teacher-schools-udise** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Schools with no teacher at all
- *Why no figure exists:* UDISE+ reports zero-ENROLMENT schools and never zero-TEACHER schools. No zero-teacher count appears in any edition 2019-20 through 2024-25, although the school-level teacher count from which it falls out is collected for every school.
- *What would close it:* A UDISE+ table counting schools with zero teachers, derivable from data the Ministry already holds

**single-teacher-schools-udise** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* The split between deployment improvement and school closure in the fall in single-teacher schools
- *Why no figure exists:* Single-teacher schools fell by 17,347 across three years while total schools fell by about 5,000 and zero-enrolment schools by 4,631. No source distinguishes how much of the reduction is a second teacher arriving from how much is the school ceasing to exist.

**single-teacher-schools-udise** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Any all-India single-teacher school figure for 2016-17 to 2021-22
- *Why no figure exists:* DISE stopped publishing after 2015-16 and UDISE+ did not begin the indicator until 2022-23 - a six-year hole spanning most of T1 in the sharpest deployment indicator there is. That CETE could compute it from 2021-22 microdata is itself evidence the data existed and was simply not published.
- *What would close it:* A research-access request to DoSEL for UDISE+ school-level files, 2016-17 to 2021-22. CETE's computation of 9.5 per cent from the 2021-22 microdata establishes both that the data exists and that access has precedent.

**teacher-vacancy-rate-ssa** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* A national all-levels vacancy figure after FY2024-25, and any figure at all in a parliamentary answer after February 2024
- *Why no figure exists:* The Department continues to compute the quantity - it furnished the 2023-24 and 2024-25 totals to the Standing Committee on 07.01.2025, printed in the 368th Report - while answering every parliamentary question since with the Concurrent List formulation and teachers in position from UDISE+. It exists and is producible under compulsion; it is not being published in answer.
- *What would close it:* A tabled parliamentary answer carrying sanctioned, in-position and vacant posts

**contract-teachers-share-government** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* A national regular-versus-non-regular teacher share published by the Government of India
- *Why no figure exists:* The UDISE+ Data Capture Format records, for every individual teacher record in the country, field 3.3.12 'Nature of Appointment: 1-Regular, 2-Contract, 3-Part-Time/Guest', identically worded in the 2022-23 and 2025-26 editions - so the data is collected exhaustively and withheld from publication, not absent. No UDISE+ report, PIB release, Economic Survey chapter or parliamentary reply publishes the national share. The Standing Committee asked for it and received the Concurrent-List non-answer that also covers vacancies.
- *What would close it:* A UDISE+ table aggregating field 3.3.12, which requires no new collection

**contract-teachers-share-government** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* The trained share of contract teachers after 2015-16
- *Why no figure exists:* DISE published it separately through 2015-16 (54-67 per cent against 79-82 for regular teachers). UDISE+ collects both the qualification field and the appointment field and publishes neither cross-tab; CETE could not compute it for 2021-22 from the public release.
- *What would close it:* An RTI to DoSEL for the UDISE+ cross-tabulation of teacher qualification against appointment type, 2016-17 onward, or the teacher-level file carrying both fields. DISE published the cross-tab through 2015-16.

**edu-spend-gdp-edu-depts** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Education spending as a share of GDP for FY2022-23 onward
- *Why no figure exists:* The Analysis of Budgeted Expenditure on Education, an annual Ministry of Education publication running since at least 2000-01, has published no edition covering FY2022-23 or later. The underlying data plainly still exists and is still compiled, since the Ministry answers on it in Parliament. Whether an edition exists and is merely unlinked - making this link-rot rather than a lapse - could not be excluded: neither the ministry's runtime API nor an Indian-IP retrieval was attempted.
- *What would close it:* An ABE edition covering FY2022-23 onward, or the ministry's runtime API queried from an Indian IP

**edu-spend-gdp-edu-depts** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* A corrected pre-FY2011-12 series on the 2011-12 GDP base for this narrow numerator
- *Why no figure exists:* The broad series was recomputed onto the 2011-12 base and its pre-splice years are 0.16 to 0.29 points too high. The narrow series' FY2000-01 to FY2010-11 rows are equally spliced and equally overstated, and no corrected value exists in any retrieved source. Since the narrow series' UPA peak of 3.22 per cent is used to say the level has never been regained, that claim rests on an uncorrected number.
- *What would close it:* Recomputation from ABE numerators against Economic Survey Statistical Appendix Table 1.6 denominators - computable, simply not yet done

**edu-spend-gdp-all-depts** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* The cause of the doubling in 'other departments' education spending across FY2013-14 and FY2014-15
- *Why no figure exists:* The break is real and in the published data - it reconciles exactly against Table 4's own columns - and it sits on the UPA-to-T1 boundary. Candidate mechanisms (a change in which ministries were counted, a reclassification of ICDS or mid-day-meal spending, a change in what training captured, or genuine expansion) were not tested, and the ABE's ministry lists were only verified stable between the 2022 and 2024 editions, a decade too late to bear on it.
- *What would close it:* The ABE editions covering FY2012-13 to FY2015-16, and their Statement 1 ministry lists

**edu-spend-gdp-centre-edu-depts** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Centre education-department spending as a share of GDP for FY2022-23 onward
- *Why no figure exists:* The Analysis of Budgeted Expenditure on Education has published no edition covering FY2022-23 or later, so the column terminates with the table it sits in. The Department holds the underlying budget figures and the series is a twenty-five-year annual publication, so this is a lapse in publication rather than an absence of data.
- *What would close it:* An ABE edition covering FY2022-23 onward

**edu-spend-gdp-centre-edu-depts** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* A corrected pre-FY2011-12 Centre series on the 2011-12 GDP base
- *Why no figure exists:* The denominator is spliced across three GDP bases by the source itself, without a note, so the pre-FY2011-12 rows sit on a different denominator from the rows after them. No recomputed series on a single base has been published for this column any more than for the totals.

**higher-ed-enrolment** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* A national higher-education dropout, retention or completion rate
- *Why no figure exists:* Every AISHE report from 2014-15 to 2023-24 was searched for dropout, retention, completion rate and transition rate: zero occurrences in every report. AISHE publishes a stock (enrolment) and an annual flow (out-turn, 1.1 crore in FY2023-24) but never links a cohort from entry to exit, and UDISE+ covers school education only. India has no published higher-education completion or dropout rate at all.
- *What would close it:* A cohort-linked AISHE module, or linkage of the existing enrolment and out-turn returns by institution and year

**higher-ed-enrolment** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Institutional finance and per-student expenditure
- *Why no figure exists:* AISHE states it collects financial information on receipts and expenditure under various heads and that per-student expenditure will be calculated, and the 2024-25 reference dates confirm it is still being collected. No AISHE report from 2012-13 to 2023-24 contains an education-finance chapter or a per-student expenditure figure. Collected for fourteen years and never published.
- *What would close it:* An RTI to DoHE for AISHE's receipts-and-expenditure aggregates and any per-student expenditure computation, 2012-13 onward. AISHE's own stated methodology establishes both are collected.

**higher-ed-enrolment** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* AISHE respondent-level microdata
- *Why no figure exists:* What is published is the report PDF, aggregate Excel tables and an institution directory. There is no anonymised respondent-level file of the kind NSS and PLFS release.
- *What would close it:* A research-access request to DoHE for anonymised AISHE respondent-level files. NSS and PLFS release unit-level data under a stated policy; AISHE has no equivalent, which is the ask.

**ugc-provision-gross** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* UGC's gross provision, Actual, for FY2024-25 onward
- *Why no figure exists:* From FY2024-25 UGC's provision is split between the Consolidated Fund of India and the Madhyamik and Uchchatar Shiksha Kosh, and the demand documents stopped showing the MUSK sub-lines. The Notes on Demands for Grants 2026-27 give Actual FY2024-25 as 3,678.47 crore, which is the Consolidated Fund component alone and is not a gross figure; the MUSK-routed component for that year was not retrieved from any primary source, and indiabudget.gov.in did not resolve on attempt (P-70). Gross for FY2024-25 exists only as BE 4,500.00 and RE 5,048.59. The money was spent, so the quantity exists in the accounts and is producible; what is absent is a published gross total.
- *What would close it:* The MUSK-routed UGC component for FY2024-25, from the Expenditure Profile MUSK statement or a Detailed Demand showing both sub-lines

**literacy-rate-7plus** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* A complete enumeration of literacy since 2011
- *Why no figure exists:* Census 2021 was never fielded. The intent notification S.O. 2681(E) of 16 June 2025 supersedes S.O. 1455(E) of 2019 and sets Census 2027 with a reference date of 1 March 2027; House Listing Operations were in month five of six on 1 August 2026, Population Enumeration - which is where the literacy question sits - is not yet notified, and the gazette notification defining the Census 2027 literacy question does not yet exist. Literacy HAS been measured recently on a sample basis; what is missing is the enumeration. A sample gives no sub-district granularity (every district- and block-level literacy plan runs on 2011 geography), no small-group disaggregation at fine geography, and no population denominators - surveys give rates, the Census gives the counts of illiterate persons that programmes are sized against. By publication this will be a 16-to-18-year interval, the longest since the Indian census series began in 1881.
- *What would close it:* Population Enumeration under Census 2027, provisional results plausibly Q2 2027 and final about 2029 on the 2011 precedent

**rte-quota-children** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* How much section 12(1)(c) money actually reached schools
- *Why no figure exists:* The Ministry states plainly that 'the Central share is released to State/UTs based on approved funding pattern and not intervention wise'. The Centre therefore does not know, and cannot report, how much money reached schools under the provision. Approval is not release and release is not payment to schools.

**teacher-vacancy-rate-elementary** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Any national vacancy figure after FY2024-25
- *Why no figure exists:* Parliamentary answers since February 2024 carry no sanctioned or vacancy number. The Department still computes the quantity and furnished it to the Standing Committee in January 2025, so it is producible under compulsion.
- *What would close it:* A tabled parliamentary answer, or publication of a sanctioned-post field in UDISE+

**india-china-imports-chinese-basis** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* China's reported exports to India for calendar 2025
- *Why no figure exists:* China had filed no calendar-2025 annual return with UN Comtrade as at 4 August 2026. Confirmed by relaxing the query one restriction at a time: relaxing the partner from India to the world, and to the United States, left the result at zero; relaxing the reporter from China to India returned a full 2025 return. The restriction that flips the zero is the period, and the finding is therefore China's non-reporting of 2025 in general, not an India-specific gap.
- *What would close it:* China's calendar-2025 annual submission to UN Comtrade, or the General Administration of Customs of China's own annual statistics for 2025.

**jk-detenus-psi** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Which preventive-detention statute each detenu is held under
- *Why no figure exists:* No table in any Prison Statistics India volume from 2011 to 2022 disaggregates detenus by law. The one chapter that classifies inmates by the law they are held under - Chapter 5 'Prisoners - Offence wise' in the current format, Chapter 4 in the pre-2016 format - is titled and scoped to convicts and undertrials only and has no detenu equivalent. NCRB names the J&K Public Safety Act exactly once, in a footnote to Tables 2.18 and 2.19 that reads 'Detenues includes inmates detained under preventive laws such as COFEPSAA, NDPS, NSA, PSA, PIT, NDPS, PBMSECA etc.', with no figures attached; the volume's own Glossary defines a detenu by reference to unnamed 'relevant preventive laws' and names no statute. Whether the State returns NCRB compiles carry law-wise detail that NCRB aggregates away is untested, and that is the difference between not-collected and not-published for this item.
- *What would close it:* A request to the Director, NCRB, for the proforma issued to States and UTs for compiling the prison returns, which would show whether law-wise detenu detail is collected and discarded or never asked for.

**jk-detenus-psi** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* The State whose authority detained each out-of-State detenu, cross-tabulated against the State holding them
- *Why no figure exists:* PSI attributes an inmate to the State whose prisons hold the body - stated once in the whole volume, in the Chapter 2 narrative, as 'the State ... where they are incarcerated' - and Table 2.12B publishes an aggregate 'Belongs to other State' column that does not name which other State. Uttar Pradesh held zero out-of-State detenus at 31 December 2018 and 188 at 31 December 2019; Haryana held 27 of whom none were Haryana-domiciled. The origin attribution exists in official hands twice over: a prison cannot lawfully hold a detenu whose detaining authority it cannot identify, and the J&K Home Department produced a year-wise out-of-territory transfer series on a single sheet in August 2023.
- *What would close it:* A request to the Director, NCRB, for Table 2.12B disaggregated by State of domicile rather than by the binary 'other State' - the origin-destination matrix underlying a column NCRB already publishes. Failing that, an RTI to the Director General (Prisons), Uttar Pradesh, for the number of detenus held in UP prisons on the orders of authorities in Jammu and Kashmir, year-wise.

**jk-detenus-psi** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Interstate transfers of detenus
- *Why no figure exists:* Chapter 7 of Prison Statistics India carries transfer counts for convicts (Table 7.1, 1,713 in 2021) and for undertrials (Table 7.3, 10,641 in 2021), and the Chapter 7 narrative has a 'Transfers' heading for both. Table 7.5 'Detenues Released' has four release columns and no transfer column, and the Chapter 7 detenu narrative has a 'Releases' heading and no 'Transfers' heading. Detenus are the one inmate class whose movement between States PSI does not count, and they are the class the J&K administration moved.

**jk-prison-detained-category** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* A year-wise count of persons detained under the Jammu and Kashmir Public Safety Act
- *Why no figure exists:* The Ministry of Home Affairs has produced PSA-identified point figures on request - detention orders against 444 persons and 389 in PSA detention on 5 February 2020, and 396 in PSA detention on 11 March 2020 - and has never produced a series. It tabled this all-laws series for 2014 to 2019 and no PSA equivalent. The J&K Home Department disclosed 1,003 persons detained between 4 March 2016 and August 2017 in answer to RTI applications, and produced a five-year year-wise series of PSA detenus transferred out of the territory on 31 August 2023; a body cannot count which detenus it moved without counting detenus. Every detention order carries a district-year serial number, so the count exists in every district office in J&K. No body has stated any reason for the omission.
- *What would close it:* A parliamentary question to the Ministry of Home Affairs for the year-wise number of persons detained under the J&K Public Safety Act since 2016 and, separately, the number of detention orders issued, with the definition of each. The definitional rider is what makes the route worth filing: the bare number would reproduce the confusion between persons and orders. The route has worked in kind - MHA answered the PSA-identified 396-of-451 split on 11 March 2020.

**jk-psa-detenus-transferred-out** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Deaths of J&K detenus in prisons outside Jammu and Kashmir
- *Why no figure exists:* NCRB's custodial-death chapter is police custody and lock-up only, with the State or UT police as its unit of account, so a J&K PSA detenu who dies in a prison in another State is a judicial-custody death attributed, if anywhere, to that State and severed from J&K entirely. One such death is documented - a Jamaat-e-Islami detenu who died in Naini jail, Prayagraj, on 23 December 2019 having been in prison since July that year, whose family was informed only after he died - and no instrument has a cell in which it can be recorded as a J&K figure.

**jk-published-suspension-orders** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* The originating suspension directions issued by the Authorized Officer
- *Why no figure exists:* On every one of the five substantive J&K orders read in full, spanning January 2020 to January 2025 and both statutory regimes, the document that directs the service providers to suspend is a police order of the Inspector General or Additional Director General of Police as Authorized Officer, and the document published is the Home Department's confirmation of it. Rule 3(2) of the 2024 Rules requires any suspension order issued under sub-rule (1) to be published, and sub-rule (1) is the provision under which the Authorized Officer acts. No originating order was located in any archive. Whether publishing the confirmation discharges the rule is a legal question this record does not answer; that it is what happens is established from primary documents.
- *What would close it:* A request to the Ministry of Home Affairs, which is the holder of the power in a Union Territory whose Public Order and Police lie outside the elected Assembly's competence, for the directions issued by Authorized Officers under rule 3(1) in Jammu and Kashmir since 22 November 2024. A route naming the J&K Home Department's website is not a route: that domain no longer resolves.

**jk-terrorist-incidents-legacy** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* What the pre-2021-22 'Incidents' figures counted
- *Why no figure exists:* MHA performed the restatement and published no note. The 2018 fall of 197 and the 2019 fall of 339 against no change at all in 2020 rule out a uniform rescaling, and the obvious candidate - law-and-order and stone-pelting events - is ruled out by MHA's own later reply.
- *What would close it:* A parliamentary question to MHA for the definitional basis of the 'Incidents' figures published in the Annual Reports up to 2020-21 and the reason for their revision in the Annual Report 2021-22.

**jk-terrorist-incidents-merged** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* The decomposition of this composite for any year before 2018
- *Why no figure exists:* MHA publishes the two components only from the Annual Report 2022-23 and only from 2018 onward. For every earlier year the composite cannot be separated, so the years the series is most often quoted across cannot be decomposed at all.
- *What would close it:* A parliamentary question to MHA for the year-wise split of terrorist-initiated incidents and encounters or counter-terror operations for 2010 to 2017, on the basis used in the Annual Report 2022-23 onward.

**jk-terrorist-initiated-incidents** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Any definition of a Terrorist Initiated Incident
- *Why no figure exists:* Neither this column nor its companion is defined anywhere in seventeen report years, so every comparison of MHA's incident count with another instrument's is a comparison in which one side's definition is unknown.
- *What would close it:* An RTI to the Ministry of Home Affairs, Department of Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh Affairs, for the instructions or proforma issued to the UT of J&K for compiling the terrorist-violence returns reproduced in the Annual Report.

**jk-encounters-ct-ops** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* The number of cordon-and-search operations conducted in J&K
- *Why no figure exists:* No published count was found from MHA, the J&K Police or the Army, in any document, for any year, by two independent searches; the string 'cordon' appears zero times in seven MHA Annual Reports and the J&K Police website publishes no statistical report of any kind. No body has been asked on the record and refused, and none has explained the omission. This is the most common form of contact between the security forces and the civilian population, and the instrument counts the outcomes of an activity it does not count. Recorded at the strength of a negative proved by absence of evidence: an operation requiring deployment orders and after-action returns is unlikely to be genuinely uncounted internally, which argues for not-published, but nothing was found either way.
- *What would close it:* An RTI to the Director General of Police, Jammu and Kashmir, and separately to the Ministry of Defence in respect of Rashtriya Rifles and Army formations, for the year-wise number of cordon-and-search operations conducted. The correct addressee designation could not be verified because the J&K Police web presence was unreachable in this phase.

**jk-encounters-ct-ops** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* What these operations produced - civilians killed in them separately from the composite column, magisterial inquiries ordered, completed or published, and AFSPA section 7 sanction requests arising
- *Why no figure exists:* The J&K chapter of the Annual Report 2024-25 contains zero occurrences of 'human right', 'NHRC', 'custody', 'custodial', 'compensation', 'ex-gratia', 'inquiry' or 'magisterial' across roughly 46,000 characters. MHA's annual accounting of the conflict contains no accountability vocabulary of any kind, so an instrument counting 731 operations has no term for their consequences.
- *What would close it:* A parliamentary question to MHA for the year-wise number of magisterial inquiries ordered into deaths in security-force operations in J&K, the number completed, and the number whose reports were published.

**jk-civilians-killed-composite** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* The two components of this column, published separately
- *Why no figure exists:* MHA's own footnote states that the figure contains civilians killed in terrorist-initiated incidents and civilians killed in encounter or counter-terrorism operations. It has never published the split, so a reader cannot recover what share of the total the state caused.
- *What would close it:* A parliamentary question to MHA asking for the two components of the 'Civilians killed' column disaggregated, using the AR 2023-24 footnote as the hook since it concedes the column is composite.

**jk-security-forces-killed** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Which forces are inside the 'Security Forces killed' column
- *Why no figure exists:* The composition has never been stated in any of seventeen report years, and the silent revision of the 2012 figure from 15 to 38 with incidents unchanged implies it has changed at least once without disclosure.
- *What would close it:* A parliamentary question to MHA for the year-wise disaggregation of security-force fatalities in J&K by force - Army and Rashtriya Rifles, each central armed police force, J&K Police and Special Police Officers.

**jk-militants-killed** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* The local and foreign composition of militants killed in J&K, for the entire post-2001 period
- *Why no figure exists:* MHA has never disaggregated this column in any Annual Report in any year, and the one instrument that published the split abandoned it on 15 November 2001, dropping with it the qualifier that its figures covered only identified militants killed. The state plainly holds something, since officials assert local and foreign shares at press conferences, but no return has ever been published and the widely-quoted split for 2024 has no retrievable basis.
- *What would close it:* A parliamentary question to MHA for the year-wise disaggregation of the 'Terrorists killed' column into local residents and foreign nationals.

**jk-militants-killed** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Whether the persons in this column were correctly identified, and in how many cases identity was later contested or established as wrong
- *Why no figure exists:* No instrument places the killing of militants beside any accounting of whether the killings were lawful, correctly identified or inquired into. The relevant counter-facts exist in different documents held by different ministries - sanction figures with the Ministry of Defence, magisterial inquiries with district administrations, the identification record with a commission now abolished - and none has ever appeared on the same page as this figure.
- *What would close it:* A parliamentary question to MHA for the year-wise number of persons recorded as terrorists killed in J&K whose identity was subsequently contested by next of kin, the number exhumed, and the number reclassified.

**jk-infiltration-attempts** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Infiltration attempts into J&K for 2023 onward
- *Why no figure exists:* MHA published this table in every Annual Report from at least 2010-11 through 2022-23 and discontinued it with no announcement and no stated reason, while the border-management apparatus that generates the count continues to operate and is described at length in the same reports. This is a termination of the instrument, not a gap in the world.
- *What would close it:* A parliamentary question to MHA for year-wise infiltration attempts and net estimated infiltration for 2023, 2024 and 2025 - a request to resume a series the Ministry itself published for over a decade. A parallel question to the Ministry of Defence would test whether the Army holds it independently.

**jk-organised-stone-pelting** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* The full year-wise organised stone-pelting series
- *Why no figure exists:* MHA holds the data and produced three sampled years on request in July 2024, but has never published a full series and has never carried the quantity in the flagship instrument at all. The omission from the Annual Report is an editorial choice rather than a data gap.
- *What would close it:* A parliamentary question to MHA for the full year-wise organised stone-pelting and hartal series - the identical route that produced the reply of 24 July 2024, which is the strongest route in this phase because it has already worked once.

**jkccs-civilians-killed-by-armed-forces** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Perpetrator attribution for civilian deaths in J&K after 2019
- *Why no figure exists:* The only body that ever published it ceased to publish; its domain has been repurposed, its coordinator has been in custody since November 2021 and a named researcher was arrested in March 2023. No official instrument has ever carried the quantity, and no successor was identified in this phase.
- *What would close it:* A dedicated assessment of Kashmir Law and Justice Project, which was publishing monthly human-rights briefings as recently as April 2026 and is the only identified live candidate successor; failing that, a registered ACLED export, which can in principle carry perpetrator attribution for India from 1 January 2016.

**epfo-net-additions** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* First-time entrants to formal payroll, separated from re-joiners and job-switchers
- *Why no figure exists:* EPFO publishes net additions, not a new-hire count, and India maintains no establishment-level longitudinal payroll register that would allow the separation.
- *What would close it:* A payroll-linked new-hire register of the kind most comparable economies maintain

**eshram-registrations** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Benefits actually delivered to e-Shram registrants
- *Why no figure exists:* Registration counts are published; downstream benefit delivery against those registrations is not reported as a series.
- *What would close it:* Scheme-linked disbursement data keyed to e-Shram identifiers

**lfpr-female** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Whether rising female participation is paid market entry, reclassified unpaid work, or distress entry
- *Why no figure exists:* PLFS counts unpaid helpers as employed and has no instrument to separate the three. The ILO modelled estimate for India is about 32% against PLFS's 41.7%, which is itself a signal of definitional divergence. Reclassified never-defined to not-collected on 2026-08-01: the quantity is defined and the denominator is defined; what is missing is collection on that base, not an agreed definition.
- *What would close it:* A time-use-linked labour module, or a PLFS supplement distinguishing paid from unpaid activity within household enterprises

**bharatnet-gps** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* BharatNet functional service delivery — actual throughput and uptime per gram panchayat
- *Why no figure exists:* Only service-readiness is published; delivered service is not systematically reported.
- *What would close it:* UNMS dashboard uptime data plus per-GP throughput measurement

**household-electrification** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Actual hours of electricity supply received by households, as a continuous national series
- *Why no figure exists:* Connections are reported; supply-hours are not published as a national time series. Survey evidence (ISEP, IRES) is periodic and partial. Reclassified not-collected to not-published on 2026-08-01: periodic survey evidence exists in holders hands (ISEP, IRES), so the test of producibility under compulsion is met; what is absent is a released national series.
- *What would close it:* CEA or discom feeder-level metering aggregated nationally, or a recurring national residential energy survey

**jjm-functionality** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* National functional coverage — the share of ALL rural households receiving water to Mission standards
- *Why no figure exists:* The 76% figure is a share of CERTIFIED households, a subset of connected ones, so it cannot be combined with the 82% connection rate to yield a national figure. Reclassified never-defined to not-collected on 2026-08-01: the quantity is defined and the denominator is defined; what is missing is collection on that base, not an agreed definition.
- *What would close it:* A functionality assessment sampling all rural households rather than certified villages

**metro-network** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Metro ridership against DPR projection, as a published annual series
- *Why no figure exists:* No official series exists; the evidence comes from one-off CAG audits and academic studies.
- *What would close it:* MoHUA mandating annual actual-versus-DPR ridership publication for every operational metro

**rail-avg-speed** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Average speed after 2019
- *Why no figure exists:* The CAG series stops and no comparable published series continues it.
- *What would close it:* Indian Railways annual statistical statements, if speed is reported on a consistent basis

**farm-household-income** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Farm household income after 2018-19
- *Why no figure exists:* The Situation Assessment Survey has not been repeated. The target was set in SAS terms and can only be judged in them.
- *What would close it:* A new NSS Situation Assessment Survey of Agricultural Households

**msp-farmers-share** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* The current share of farmers selling at MSP
- *Why no figure exists:* No recurring series exists. The 6% figure is a 2015 committee estimate from 2012-13 survey data; SAS 2019 gives output shares (paddy 23.7%, wheat 20.8%) but not a farmer-count share, and nothing has been published since.
- *What would close it:* An MSP-realisation module in a future Situation Assessment Survey, or farmer-level procurement data from FCI

**pmay-g-completed** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Houses completed and actually occupied
- *Why no figure exists:* The third stage of the cascade has no public measurement; completion is reported, occupancy is not.
- *What would close it:* PMAY-G dashboard, if an occupancy field is ever published

**pmfby-farmers** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Share of PMFBY claims settled within the two-month norm
- *Why no figure exists:* No national series on settlement timeliness is published, though a 12% penalty on insurers for delay exists in the scheme rules.
- *What would close it:* Routine publication of settlement-lag statistics on the National Crop Insurance Portal

**soil-health-cards** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Whether Soil Health Card recommendations changed farmer practice
- *Why no figure exists:* Cards distributed are counted; adoption is not measured as a routine metric. Only ad-hoc academic evaluations exist. Reclassified never-defined to not-collected on 2026-08-01: the quantity is defined and the denominator is defined; what is missing is collection on that base, not an agreed definition.
- *What would close it:* A national adoption and impact survey with a defined practice-change indicator

**ujjwala-refills** (series) · `not-collected`

- *What is not measured:* Population-scale health outcomes from reduced solid-fuel exposure
- *Why no figure exists:* The scheme's stated rationale was health, but no population-level outcome study links Ujjwala to respiratory or maternal health change. Reclassified never-defined to not-collected on 2026-08-01: the quantity is defined and the denominator is defined; what is missing is collection on that base, not an agreed definition.
- *What would close it:* A cohort or difference-in-differences study on household air pollution exposure

**ujjwala-refills** (series) · `not-published`

- *What is not measured:* Refill rates after December 2018
- *Why no figure exists:* The CAG audit series stops there and no comparable published series continues it.
- *What would close it:* MoPNG refill data, if published

## E.3 — Claims about what EXISTS — 291 candidate sentences across 179 records

The rule: a claim about what exists is not a claim about what the sources contain, and only the second is checkable. *"No other body publishes this"* asserts something no retrieval can establish; *"no other publisher was located"* states the observation actually made. The mechanical test is in Extract C and it is worth restating: **could a single document, if it turned up tomorrow, falsify the sentence without any figure in the record changing?** If yes, it is a claim about existence and has to rest on what was searched.

```
NEEDLE  /\b(?:no (?:other|body|instrument|publisher|source|explanation|figure|record|agreed|equivalent)|nobody|never been published|the only|unprecedented|unexplained|not published anywhere|any government)\b/i
FIELDS  summary claimAtLaunch whatHappened caseFor caseAgainst assessmentNote caveat differentFactsNote revisitTrigger shockExposure whatChanged bridgeNote notes
SCOPE   ledger + provenance + series, sentence-split on [.!?]
```

**This is a CANDIDATE LIST and most of it will be correctly grounded.** The needle matches the phrasing, not the defect; the corpus has already rewritten several of these onto what was searched, and those rewrites match too. What is wanted is the ones where the surrounding text does not carry a search.

- **L-0066** `summary` — The only complete propose-resist-repeal arc in this record.
- **L-0067** `caseAgainst` — On the only instrument that measures what was promised, real income grew about 16% over six years against a target requiring roughly 100% over seven.
- **L-0067** `assessmentNote` — The only instrument that measures that quantity, the Situation Assessment Survey, gives about 16 per cent real growth over the six years to 2018-19 against a target requiring roughly 100 per cent over seven.
- **L-0071** `whatHappened` — Crop diversification programmes have repeatedly failed because MSP-assured paddy and wheat are the only crops with a guaranteed buyer, so farmers rationally decline to switch without an equivalent guarantee.
- **L-0071** `caseAgainst` — Three central policies — assured procurement of paddy, no equivalent guarantee for alternatives, and tolerance of free farm power — together make water-mining the rational choice for individual farmers, and no element has been altered.
- **L-0025** `assessmentNote` — Nobody disputes that recovery on written-off accounts runs at roughly 13-18 per cent, that Rs 13.91 lakh crore remains unrecovered, or that borrower liability survives the accounting entry.
- **L-0028** `assessmentNote` — The gazette was not obtained - only a private portal's reproduction of it - so no score against the scheme is supportable, and worked was resting on an objective nobody in this project has read.
- **L-0029** `assessmentNote` — It is NOT a finding that the system excluded nobody, and the exclusion question is live and unquantified in this record.
- **L-0033** `summary` — The one-time capital impact is not established here: the only figure in circulation is a T4 relay and no primary source for it has been retrieved.
- **L-0033** `caseAgainst` — On this record none of that can be sized: the directions themselves have never been retrieved and the only quantified impact in circulation is a T4 relay.
- **L-0090** `caseAgainst` — There is no causal identification and nobody claims one: the mission launched nationally and simultaneously, with no untreated comparison group, no staggered adoption and no discontinuity, and the FLN implementation questions were asked for the first time in 2024, so no difference-in-differences of any kind is possible.
- **L-0093** `summary` — No back-cast, no dual-basis year and no reconciliation exists, so how much of the fall is deduplication and how much is real decline has never been published.
- **L-0093** `caseAgainst` — The one number that would let anyone read the reform - how much of 1.72 crore was ghosts and how much was children - has never been published, and the Ministry holds both bases and could produce a dual run for a single year.

- **L-0097** `caseAgainst` — Eight years after the notification the remediation is still running, with registration open to August 2026 and non-completion invalidating the appointment, so a cohort of serving primary teachers holds employment conditional on a course they have not yet finished - and nobody has counted them.
- **L-0097** `caveat` — UDISE+'s 'professionally qualified' is not a compliance rate with RTE section 23 and overstates it at primary level by a margin nobody has measured.
- **L-0099** `caseAgainst` — And the national pattern removes the innocent explanations: no other state saw anything comparable in the same years, so this was a rule change and not a demand shift, a pandemic effect, or a reporting artefact.

- **L-0101** `caveat` — The Article 131 suit is weaker still: the only account of it retrieved is a paywall-truncated news report, the plaint is not public, and the Supreme Court's case-status register is CAPTCHA-gated, so the suit's diary number and filing date could not be confirmed and are not stated here.
- **L-0102** `caseAgainst` — And the improvement itself is unexplained: other-departments education spending grew 41.7 then 49.0 per cent across FY2013-14 and FY2014-15, roughly doubling in two years, exactly at the political transition, against 11.4 and 8.4 per cent for education departments - and no retrieved document accounts for it.
- **L-0102** `caseAgainst` — Both terminal points are Budget Estimates, which revise down by about 0.35 points to Actual on the only year where all three stages exist, and the Union underspent its own budget in 13 of 16 completed years.

- **L-0102** `caveat` — It is simultaneously the series Parliament is briefed on, the series compared against the 6 per cent target, and the only one of the two that shows improvement across the transition - and the improvement is driven by that doubling.

- **L-0061** `caseAgainst` — The 60-day strike notice constrains the only leverage workers hold.
